newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slower Slovak output growth no threat to GDP.
newsitem.headline: Slower Slovak output growth no threat to GDP.

text.p: A lower-than-expected rise in Slovak industrial output in March should not have a significant influence on overall GDP growth, analysts said on Tuesday.

The Slovak Statistical Bureau (SUSR) said March industrial output rose 1.5 percent year-on-year, down from a 2.2 percent rise in February. A Reuters poll of analysts on Monday predicted March output may increase by as much as four percent.
"...the slower (output) increase will probably not endanger GDP growth since a major part of it should be boosted by services, just as it was in 1996," ING Barings analyst Martin Barto told Reuters.
He added low output growth should continue in the coming months, since the pace of restructuring of small and medium-sized firms was an obstacle to its acceleration.
Juraj Rencko, chief macroeconomic analyst at the Slovak Academy of Science, noted that problems on the export side of the economy were another important factor behind slower growth of output.

"There are several factors behind the slow growth, such as the economy's structural aspects, a stronger crown and rising wages, which altogether make our exports less competitive than in previous years," Rencko said.

Slovakia exports only a narrow range of value-added goods such as oil products or cars from Volkswagen's Bratislava plant, with semi-finished materials accounting for a major part of the overall exports.
"It's sometimes hard to find room for such products on highly competitive target markets -- the EU and the Czech Republic," he added.

The Slovak economy is strongly linked to the development of its main export partners since its small domestic market -- 5.5 million people -- does not create enough demand for strong sustained economic growth.
Rencko said he saw average industrial production rising between 3.0 to 3.5 percent in the first half of 1997.

"I am optimistic for industrial growth in the near future since the central bank's restrictive measures are already bringing results to the trade balance. The budget also showed positive development in the three months of 1996," he said.
